findings.reason: a builder handed this must either suffix every round (breaking the stated first-round id and the "strips a trailing head suffix" reader contract it assumes) or invent an unstated way to tell round one from later rounds; the plan does not say how the round is distinguished, so the node is sent to guess at the one branch its whole change turns on.
findings.text: §3 says "A first round keeps today's id" while also saying the shared head-keyed rule (`<prefix><source>-<head[:12]>`, the rule `repair_node_id` applies) "is applied there" in `reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py`, where the run-review id is composed as `f"{REVIEW_NODE_PREFIX}{source_node}"`; but that composition site (`_review_dispatch_fields`, line ~652) resolves the run's head unconditionally (`head = _run_head_for_review(record)`, line ~607) and takes no round history, and the named rule suffixes whenever a head resolves — so a first round cannot "keep today's id" and a later round cannot be distinguished from it at that site
